questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: An English speaking country, and high academic level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the university in Melbourne has a comprehensive program for exchange students which you are enrolled in from ealy on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mails and invitations to online meetings with the university. Mostly regarding visa, accomondation and application at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Accomondations with different levels of sharing with others; there were many different options and definitely something for everyone. Although it was a bit expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A new and well equipped kitchen was avaiable in the appartments and two bigger shared kitchens were available for everyone.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is a bit more expensive than off campus, however it is more convenient and where I stayed (The Lofts) there was a lot of activities planned to get to know the other residents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied only for classes open for all, so I did not need any specific classes in advance. After you have been approved for a class, you choose when you take the classes as they are often offered multiple times a week. This was a great posibility to plan flexibility into my week.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a coordinator avaiable for all exchange students. I did not have the need contact him.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very; I got all my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: This process was also very smooth for me as I went with only my fully elective classes. I would you say apply for approval in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of education was at the lower side compared to KU. The fact that I could without problems follow business and social classes without any prior knowledge, tells something about the level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was very similar; physical classes and expercises. The main difference was that all classes got recorded so I could watch it afterwards.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Politics of Food
HR Fundamentals
Leadership in Science
Data and Decision Making

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Politics of Food. It raised many relevant issues with the food system of today, and the teacher was engaging and a little provocrative.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No, only that I went on many trips during the semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was a bit more expensive than I expected and the overall level is very similar to Denmark, jsut a little cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. The university is so big that it basically offers everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went the running club on Fridays, good vibes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Make the time to see Melbourne and Tasmania, Sydney also!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the culture is not that different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to class and a club. There are many other national or exchange students, so sometimes it is a bit difficult to find the locals - especially on the MA.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing challenging really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The acklowledgement of the First Nation. It is just beginning to be part of the everyday, and I find it very interesting after 200 years.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) show up - for classes, clubs, activities
2) ask for help if you need it - they are very helpful here
3) live on campus - it gives you so many great opportunities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to meet not only locals but a lot of Indians and Chinese.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Engaging with other cultures and learning about a new country from a European perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To always be surrounded by people and to balance the need to relax with the urge to see everything.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
